experiment: Earlier emission by delay-penalized fine-tuning of the 20M streaming Zipformer, with and without zero-fill previews
motivation: On the public 20M model the native display delay (458/463ms) splits into an emission lag of 238/236ms after the aligned word end and 220/228ms of chunk wait plus lookahead. Zero-fill previews at k=7 emit tokens correctly (0.89-0.98) in encoder frames that contain no real audio, so most of the lag is a learned habit, not missing evidence.

hypotheses.H1: Fine-tuning with a k2 delay penalty lowers the emission lag by at least 100ms at a WER cost of at most 0.5 points absolute on the 400-utterance dev subset.
hypotheses.H2: Zero-fill previews and the delay penalty consume the same lag: the preview gain (none minus k7) shrinks as the penalty grows.
hypotheses.H0_control: Fine-tuning with penalty 0 leaves lag and WER unchanged.

train_data: LibriSpeech train-clean-100, features as in predict_correct_v1/prepare.py
loss: 0.5 * smoothed simple RNN-T + pruned RNN-T (prune range 5, lm scale 0.25), delay_penalty passed to both
optimizer: ScaledAdam lr 0.002 constant, clipping scale 2.0, no SpecAugment, fp32, at most 50000 feature frames per batch
evaluation: Fixed 200 dev-clean + 200 dev-other subset and alignments of preview_filler_v1; streaming replay in PyTorch; every encoder pass charged 5.0ms; previews zero-filled at k=7,15,23; test unused
compute: USC CARC Discovery, one GPU per arm
